title: Overlabels Recipe Manifest
description: Declarative description of a Recipe: the things it installs into an account (overlays, integration connections), the primitives it wires together (option sets, pickers), the controls it exports, and the triggers that fire its pickers. Manifests are 100% declarative - no executable code - because they are intended to be Claude-auditable before publishing.

recipe_format_version.description: The schema version this manifest targets. The installer rejects formats it does not understand.

slug.description: Globally unique identifier for the recipe. Becomes part of [[[c:<slug>:<instance>:<name>]]] tag namespace; snake_case only.

version.description: Integer version. A new version is a new installable artifact, never an in-place upgrade.

description.description: Short blurb shown on the recipe's install page.

icon_url.description: URL to an icon image (PNG/JPG/WebP). Optional.

changelog.description: Notes on what changed in this version.

min_overlabels_version.description: Minimum platform schema version this manifest needs. Increments only on breaking changes to the recipe-format itself.

requires_integrations.description: List of external integration source keys this recipe reads controls from (e.g. ['kofi', 'streamlabs']). Installer warns but does not block when an installer lacks one of these.

max_instances_per_user.description: Per-user install cap for this recipe. Defaults to platform-wide admin setting if omitted.

listed.description: Whether the recipe is shown on the public /products page as an installable product. Unlisted recipes can still be installed by a seeder or tinker.

requires_bot.description: Whether the installed result only works with the Overlabels bot in the streamer's chat. Drives the human steps on the product page: it is not something the installer can do.

hero.description: Site-relative path of a 16:9 hero image shown above the product on the /products listing. Lives under public/products/. Optional.

notes.description: Short plain-text lines shown on the product page after install, for the optional things the installer does not decide for the streamer.

installs.description: Rows the installer creates in the account beyond the picker primitives: overlays from markdown files shipped next to the manifest, and integration connections. Everything here is idempotent per install and belongs to the instance.

overlays.description: Overlay documents to create, in the same markdown format the import button accepts and the public .md endpoint emits. Controls the document defines are created with it.

file.description: Filename relative to the manifest's directory. No path separators.

integrations.description: External service keys to connect on install, exactly as the service's settings page would: the integration row is created enabled and its controls are provisioned.

lists.description: User Lists to create, empty, exactly as /dashboard/lists creates one. The slug is what the overlay's [[[c:list:<slug>]]] tags and the !list command name, so it is fixed by the manifest, not per instance. The install refuses if the account already has a list with that slug.

list_appenders.description: Chat commands that append to one of the lists above, exactly as the list's Appenders panel creates one. The install refuses if the command name is already taken on the account.

list.description: The ref of a list declared in installs.lists.

value.description: What gets appended. Defaults to the chatter's name, [[[bot:from_user]]].

bot_aliases.description: Bot Aliases to create, exactly as /settings/bot/aliases creates one: a short command that the bot expands to a longer one. The streamer can rename or delete them afterwards. Validated by BotAliasValidator, so the same rules apply as in the form (no chains, no self-loops, {1}/{*} placeholders only).

target.description: What the bot runs instead, e.g. '!list lane pop first'.

bot_commands.description: Custom Bot Commands to create, exactly as /settings/bot/commands creates one. Validated by BotCommandValidator, so the reply obeys the same rules as in the form, and any counter: tag it names is provisioned.

reply.description: The templated text the bot speaks.

option_sets.description: Named, reusable lists of values that pickers draw from.

pickers.description: RNG / selection engines over an option set.

control_exports.description: Maps picker state to user-facing controls. Each export becomes a [[[c:<slug>:<instance>:<name>]]] tag at install time.

triggers.description: Entry points that fire pickers (chat command, dashboard button). EventSub and scheduled triggers are deliberately out of v1.

primitiveRef.description: Manifest-local identifier for a primitive. Translated to a real DB id and per-instance slug at install time.

controlExportName.description: Name of an exported control. Lands as the third colon segment in the tag namespace.

items.description: Default items. Each item is a short string. User-editable option sets accept post-install edits within min/max bounds.

option_set_ref.description: Must match the ref of an option_set declared in the same manifest.

from.description: Dotted path to the picker state being exported. Currently only pickers.<ref>.{result|result_at|running} are supported.

fires.description: Dotted path to the picker that fires. Format: pickers.<ref>.
